messages.content: How do I stock a catfish pond?

Stocking rate and water quality are one decision, not two. Overstocking raises ammonia, stresses the fish and stunts growth no matter how well you feed. Fish gulping at the surface is a warning that the water cannot carry the load. Either exchange water more often or reduce the number of fish; feeding harder into bad water only makes it worse.
Why does it matter how I combine trees with my crops?

Trees kept deliberately in fields provide shade, fodder, fuel and, in the case of nitrogen fixing species, a real fertility contribution. The trade-off is competition for light and water, so choose species that come into leaf out of phase with the crop, and prune to manage the canopy. Done well the field carries both; done carelessly the trees win and the crop suffers.
How much water does rice need?

It depends entirely on which system you are growing in, and that is not me avoiding the question. The answer genuinely changes.

Which are you?

1. Upland rainfed, grown on ordinary sloping or flat land and depending on rain alone.
2. Lowland or fadama, in a low lying area that naturally holds water.
3. Fully irrigated with a controlled supply.

If you are lowland or irrigated, the practical guidance is to keep a shallow standing depth through tillering, and then drain the field before harvest so the ground firms up enough to work on. Continuous deep flooding is not better and wastes water.

If you are upland, you are managing rainfall rather than water depth, and your priorities move to weed control and choosing a variety suited to upland conditions. Tell me which one you are and I will be more specific.
Why does it matter how I decide which fertiliser to buy?

Buying fertiliser without testing is the most common way smallholders waste money. You pay for nutrients the soil already has while the one nutrient actually limiting your yield stays short, so the crop does not improve and the fertiliser gets blamed. A test costs far less than a season of the wrong input. Your extension officer will know where testing is available.
My cassava leaves are yellow and twisted. I sprayed insecticide twice and nothing changed. What stronger chemical should I use?

Please stop spending money on spray for this. Yellow mottled and twisted cassava leaves are cassava mosaic disease, and no insecticide, at any strength, will reverse it.

It is a virus. It is carried by whitefly, but far more importantly it is carried in the stem cuttings themselves. If you planted cuttings taken from an infected plant, the crop was infected before it ever came up, which is why spraying changed nothing.

What to do:

1. Accept this season's crop for what it is. Rogue out the worst affected plants.
2. This is the important one: never take planting material from a plant showing these symptoms. Take cuttings only from healthy vigorous plants, from the middle of stems eight to twelve months old.
3. Get improved resistant varieties if you can. TME 419 and TMS 30572 are widely grown for this reason.

Clean planting material is the whole control. Farmers who fix that one habit stop having this problem.
Can you explain cocoa farming for a beginner?

Cocoa is a staple of West and Central African smallholder systems. Harvest ripe pods regularly rather than in occasional large sweeps. Frequent harvest removes disease sources and reduces losses. Fermentation and drying decide the price you are paid. Under-fermented or smoke-tainted beans are downgraded no matter how good the tree was.
Is fall armyworm the same as the armyworm that moves in swarms?

They are different pests with similar names, and the control differs.

**Fall armyworm** stays with the crop it hatched on. It feeds inside the maize whorl, is present in the field more or less continuously once established, and is the one that leaves frass in the funnel.

**African armyworm** moves in large migrating groups, strips foliage from cereals and pasture, and appears suddenly in outbreaks after certain rainfall patterns. It feeds openly on the leaves rather than hiding in the whorl.

If the damage is inside the funnel with frass, treat it as fall armyworm. If large numbers appeared overnight and are eating leaves in the open, report it, because outbreaks are managed at district level and your extension service will want to know.
Can you explain sweet potato farming for a beginner?

Sweet potato is a staple of West and Central African smallholder systems. Lift carefully. Bruised and cut roots rot quickly in storage and do not sell. Check this against what your neighbours are seeing before you act on a whole field.
I want to store my maize until prices go up. How do I do it without chemicals?

That is a sound plan, since everyone sells at harvest and prices are at their lowest exactly when the grain is ready. Storing well is one of the few ways a smallholder captures a better price.

Two things decide whether it works:

1. Dry it properly first. Grain must be dry enough to store safely, around thirteen percent moisture. Grain that feels dry in the afternoon sun is often still too wet. Dry on a tarpaulin or raised platform, never bare ground, which puts moisture and soil straight back into it.
2. Store hermetically. Sealed bags such as PICS starve storage insects of air, which controls them without any chemical. They work extremely well, but only if you seal the liner properly every single time you open it. A bag left loosely closed is just an ordinary bag.

Check the store periodically for damp spots and for holes in grain or dust beneath the bags. If you put away grain that was not dry enough, you will find out in storage, and by then the options are poor.
How do I tell cocoa black pod apart from other problems on cocoa?

Cocoa black pod on cocoa can be identified in the field before you treat.

What to look for:
- Dark brown to black spreading lesions on pods, often starting at the tip or stalk end, in wet weather.

Harvest frequently, remove and bury or destroy infected pods, prune for an open canopy and improve drainage. Sanitation does most of the work.

What is the right way to package produce for market?

Packaging is not decoration. Grading produce into uniform sizes and packing it cleanly gets a better price for exactly the same crop, because buyers pay for predictability and reject lots they must sort themselves. It also reduces damage in transit, so more of what you grew arrives saleable.
My maize get hole for leaf and I dey see like sawdust for inside the middle. Wetin be dis?

Na fall armyworm be dat. The sawdust wey you dey see na the caterpillar poo, and if e pack for inside the whorl, e clear say na am.

Make you check first:

1. Open the middle of plenty plants, for early morning or evening time when dem dey active.
2. Look for white mark like Y for the caterpillar head.
3. Look four black dot wey stand like square near the tail.

If you see am, start with the thing wey no go cost you money. Pick the caterpillar comot with hand if the farm small. After you harvest, clear and burn the stalk, because na there the pest dey hide reach next season.

If you wan spray, use product wey dem register for fall armyworm for maize, and follow the rate wey dey for the label. Pour the spray enter the middle of the plant, no be on top leaf, because na inside the caterpillar dey.

I want to use poultry manure safely. What should I know?

Poultry manure is strong and fast acting, which cuts both ways. Fresh manure burns young plants and carries weed seed, so compost or age it before use. Applied well ahead of planting and worked in, it feeds the crop and builds organic matter at the same time, which bagged fertiliser does not do. Keep a note of what you did and when, because next season that record beats any general advice.
How do I deal with striga on my maize, sorghum, millet, upland rice?

Rotation with legumes, restoring soil fertility and organic matter, hand pulling before the weed flowers and seeds, and resistant varieties where available. Small purple or pink flowered weed emerging near cereal stems, with the crop stunted and yellowed out of proportion to the visible weed. A striga problem is a soil fertility problem. It thrives where nitrogen and organic matter are depleted.
I already did that and it did not help. What else?

Rotation with legumes, restoring soil fertility and organic matter, hand pulling before the weed flowers and seeds, and resistant varieties where available. Small purple or pink flowered weed emerging near cereal stems, with the crop stunted and yellowed out of proportion to the visible weed. When a problem returns each season the source was usually never removed, rather than the treatment having failed.

How do I stop stem borers coming back next season?
1. Destroy or plough in crop residues after harvest to break the carryover, since larvae overwinter in stalks. Early uniform planting across a community reduces pressure for everyone.

Tell me about growing cowpea.
Cowpea is a staple of West and Central African smallholder systems, known locally as ewa (Yoruba), wake (Hausa).
Why does it matter how I raise tilapia in a pond?

Tilapia breed readily in ponds, and that is the main problem rather than a benefit: the pond fills with small fish competing for feed and none reach market size. Stocking mono-sex fingerlings, or managing recruitment with a predator species, is what keeps them growing. Feed and water exchange then determine how fast.
Can you explain cassava farming for a beginner?

Cassava is a staple of West and Central African smallholder systems, known locally as ege (Yoruba), akpu (Igbo), rogo (Hausa). 1m by 1m for sole crop, about 10,000 plants per hectare. Wider at 1m by 1.5m when intercropping with maize. 9 to 12 months for early varieties, up to 18 months for late. Roots left too long become woody and lose starch quality. Process within 48 hours of harvest. Roots deteriorate fast once lifted.
I am not sure when to put my yam in the ground. Any guidance?

Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake. Milk harvest of the first tuber can be taken while the plant continues, or a single harvest at senescence. Cure tubers in shade before storing in a ventilated barn. Damaged tubers rot and spread rot to the rest. Your local extension officer can confirm which varieties and products are registered in your area.

Packaging is not decoration. Grading produce into uniform sizes and packing it cleanly gets a better price for exactly the same crop, because buyers pay for predictability and reject lots they must sort themselves. It also reduces damage in transit, so more of what you grew arrives saleable.
Tell me about growing onion.
Onion is a staple of West and Central African smallholder systems. Keep a note of what you did and when, because next season that record beats any general advice.
What goes wrong when farmers do not dry produce faster and cleaner?

A simple raised solar dryer dries faster and cleaner than open ground, and keeps rain, dust and animals off the crop. Faster drying is directly less mould and less aflatoxin risk. It can be built from local timber and clear plastic sheet, and pays for itself in one rejected consignment avoided. Conditions differ between zones and soils, so treat this as a starting point.
What is the best approach to cassava mosaic?

The main control is clean planting material and resistant varieties. Rogue out badly affected plants. There is no spray that cures an infected plant. Yellow and green mottling, distorted and reduced leaves, stunted plants. Carried by whitefly and, most importantly, by planting infected stem cuttings.
I already did that and it did not help. What else?

The main control is clean planting material and resistant varieties. Rogue out badly affected plants. There is no spray that cures an infected plant. Yellow and green mottling, distorted and reduced leaves, stunted plants. When a problem returns each season the source was usually never removed, rather than the treatment having failed.
What is the right way to feed cattle through the dry season?

Dry season feed is the binding constraint on cattle in most of the savanna, and it is a planning problem rather than an emergency. Conserve crop residues at harvest, when they are free and abundant, instead of buying feed at the peak of scarcity. An animal that loses heavy condition in the dry season spends the following wet season regaining it rather than growing.

What goes wrong when farmers do not plan a rotation?

Alternating legumes and cereals does two things at once: it breaks pest and disease cycles that build up under continuous cropping, and it leaves nitrogen behind for the following cereal. A cowpea or soybean crop before maize measurably reduces next season's fertiliser bill. Continuous maize on the same ground is what invites striga and stem borer to establish.
My yam is underperforming. Where do I start?

Seed yam of about 250 to 300g, or setts produced by the minisett technique, which multiplies planting material from a single tuber. Large mounds or ridges for drainage and tuber expansion. Compacted soil produces short, forked tubers. Milk harvest of the first tuber can be taken while the plant continues, or a single harvest at senescence. Cure tubers in shade before storing in a ventilated barn. Damaged tubers rot and spread rot to the rest.
Sorry, what does that mean exactly?

Seed yam of about 250 to 300g, or setts produced by the minisett technique, which multiplies planting material from a single tuber. Large mounds or ridges for drainage and tuber expansion. Compacted soil produces short, forked tubers. Put simply: fix the cause, not the symptom, and do the cheap thing first.

My cassava leaf dey yellow and e twist. I don spray insecticide but nothing change.

Make you stop to spend money for spray. Na cassava mosaic disease be dat, and no insecticide fit cure am.

Na virus. Whitefly dey carry am, but the main way e dey enter na through the stem wey you plant. If you cut your stem from plant wey get the sickness, the farm don carry am before e even germinate. Na why the spray no do anything.

Wetin you go do:

1. This season own don happen. Comot the plant wey bad well well.
2. This one important: no ever cut planting stem from plant wey dey show this sign. Cut from healthy strong plant, from the middle of stem wey don reach eight to twelve months.
3. Try get improved variety like TME 419 or TMS 30572 wey fit resist am.

Clean planting material na the whole control.
My cowpea is not doing well. How do I work out the problem?

On cowpea a short list of causes covers most of what goes wrong.

What to look for:
- Check for flower thrips.
- Check for pod borers.
- Check for aphids.
- Check for storage bruchids.

Match the symptom to the cause before spending money. The wrong treatment costs cash and loses the window for the right one.

What is the right way to start keeping rabbits?

Rabbits suit very small capital: they breed quickly, eat forage rather than competing with the household for grain, and need little space. The failure point is housing. Hutches must stay dry and well ventilated but out of direct sun and rain, because rabbits tolerate cold far better than heat or damp.
My maize is underperforming. Where do I start?

Moisture stress at tasselling and silking causes the largest yield loss of any stage. 75cm between rows and 25cm within rows, one plant per stand, about 53,000 plants per hectare. Split nitrogen: a basal compound fertiliser at planting, then top dress with urea at about 3 to 4 weeks, and again at knee height on poor soils. Place fertiliser in a band beside the plant, not broadcast, to cut losses. Hybrid seed yields more but must be bought fresh each season. Open pollinated varieties can be saved for 2 to 3 seasons with careful selection, which suits farmers with tight cash.

Moisture stress at tasselling and silking causes the largest yield loss of any stage. 75cm between rows and 25cm within rows, one plant per stand, about 53,000 plants per hectare. Put simply: fix the cause, not the symptom, and do the cheap thing first.
Something is wrong with my cassava and I cannot tell what. What should I check?

On cassava a short list of causes covers most of what goes wrong.

What to look for:
- Check for cassava mosaic disease.
- Check for cassava green mite.
- Check for root rot on waterlogged soil.
- Check for late weeding.

Match the symptom to the cause before spending money. The wrong treatment costs cash and loses the window for the right one.
How is plantain and banana grown?
Plantain and banana are staples of West and Central African smallholder systems, known locally as ogede (Yoruba).

Why does it matter how I dry my harvest properly?

Dry on a tarpaulin or a raised platform, never on bare ground. Ground drying puts moisture back into the crop from below, adds soil and stones that buyers reject, and exposes it to animals. A raised platform also lets air move underneath, which dries faster and more evenly.

I am not sure when to put my soybean in the ground. Any guidance?

Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake. Harvest as soon as pods are dry and rattling. Leaving it standing invites shattering, and shattered grain on the ground is lost.

My groundnuts got rained on while drying. They look fine now that they are dry. Can I still sell them?

Be careful here, because looking fine is not the same as being safe.

Groundnut that dries slowly, or gets wetted again part way through drying, is the classic route to aflatoxin. It is a mould toxin, it is not visible at levels that still matter, and it does not go away once the nuts dry out. It causes real harm to people and animals, and it is the usual reason a consignment gets rejected at a formal buyer.

What I would do:

1. Sort hard. Discard every nut that is shrivelled, discoloured, mouldy or damaged. That sorting removes a large share of the risk.
2. Get them fully dry now and keep them dry, in ventilated storage off the ground.
3. If you are selling to a buyer who tests, ask about testing before you commit a large quantity.

For future harvests the defence is speed. Lift, dry fast on a tarpaulin or raised platform rather than bare ground, and get them under cover before rain. Once the toxin is there, there is nothing you can add to remove it.
I want to deworm my small ruminants. What should I know?

Worm burden rises sharply in the wet season when larvae survive on pasture, so timing matters more than which product you use. Deworming on a fixed schedule with the same product year after year breeds resistance. Ask your veterinary or extension officer what is working locally, and rotate products rather than repeating one. Your local extension officer can confirm which varieties and products are registered in your area.
How often should I check my maize for fall armyworm?

Scout weekly from emergence until the crop tassels, and pay most attention in the first few weeks, because that is when the pest costs you real yield.

How to do it properly:

1. Walk a W or X pattern across the field rather than checking the edge, since infestation is patchy.
2. Open the whorl on about twenty plants spread over that path.
3. Count how many of the twenty have live larvae or fresh moist frass. Old dry damage with no larvae does not count.
4. Go early morning or late evening. In the heat of the day the larvae sit deep and you will miss them.

That count is what tells you whether to act. Treating on the sight of a single caterpillar wastes money; ignoring a heavy early infestation costs the crop.
When I go plant my maize?

No plant when the first rain fall. Wait make the rain settle well well.

Plenty farmer dey rush plant when the first rain drop, then sun come out for one week and the seed die. Na so dem go plant again, and that one na money wey waste.

Wetin you go do: wait till rain don fall steady for some days and ground don wet reach down. Na then you go plant. For spacing, make am 75cm between the rows and 25cm between each plant, one plant for each hole.

If you no sure about the rain for your area this year, ask your extension officer or the older farmers wey dey your village. Dem sabi the pattern pass any general advice.
I want to keep backyard chickens profitably. What should I know?

Backyard flocks give the best return on very small capital, because the birds scavenge much of their own feed. The catch is that unvaccinated local flocks are periodically wiped out by Newcastle disease, which erases years of slow gains in a fortnight. Keeping vaccination up, and supplementing scavenging with a little grain, turns a fragile flock into a reliable one. Do the cheapest thing on this list first and give it two weeks before spending more.

Which crops suit the sudan zone?

Single season, roughly 500 to 1000mm. Sorghum, millet, cowpea, groundnut, some maize with fertiliser. Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake.
What should I focus on to improve my sweet potato?

Use vine cuttings about 30cm long taken from healthy vigorous vines, planted into ridges or mounds. Ridges or mounds give the roots room to size up and keep them out of waterlogged soil. Lift carefully. Bruised and cut roots rot quickly in storage and do not sell.
Is it too late in the season to do that now?

Use vine cuttings about 30cm long taken from healthy vigorous vines, planted into ridges or mounds. Ridges or mounds give the roots room to size up and keep them out of waterlogged soil. Judge it against an untreated patch after a fortnight rather than by eye the next morning.

Walk me through planting oil palm on a small plot.

1. About 9m triangular spacing, roughly 143 palms per hectare. Crowded palms shade each other and yield falls.
2. Plant tenera hybrid seedlings from a reputable source. Dura palms grown from random seed give much thicker shells and less oil.
I am not sure when to put my sweet potato in the ground. Any guidance?

Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake. Lift carefully. Bruised and cut roots rot quickly in storage and do not sell. Keep a note of what you did and when, because next season that record beats any general advice.
Dem tell me say na stem borer dey my maize but the sawdust dey for the middle of the plant, no be for the stem.

If the sawdust dey for the middle of the plant, for inside the funnel where new leaf dey come out, na fall armyworm, no be stem borer.

How dem take different:

1. Fall armyworm dey chop for inside the whorl, the middle. You go see hole wey scatter for the young leaf, and the frass wey wet dey pack for centre.
2. Stem borer dey bore enter the stem. You go see small hole for the stem with dry frass for the mouth of the hole, and sometimes the middle shoot go die while the outside leaf still green.

The reason e matter: fall armyworm, spray fit reach am if you pour am enter the whorl. Borer wey don enter stem, spray no fit reach am at all, so na clearing residue after harvest be the main thing.
How do I brood day old chicks?

Brooding decides how a broiler batch turns out, and chick behaviour tells you the temperature better than a thermometer does. Huddling under the heat source means too cold; spread to the walls and panting means too hot; evenly spread and feeding means correct. Start warm in week one and step the temperature down each week as they feather. Cold chicks in the first week never fully catch up, whatever you feed them afterwards. Ask the older farmers in your area what has worked there, since local experience beats a general rule.

How is groundnut grown?
Groundnut is a staple of West and Central African smallholder systems, known locally as epa (Yoruba), gyada (Hausa).

There are ragged holes in my young maize and something wet and grainy sitting in the funnel of the plant.

That is fall armyworm. The wet grainy material in the funnel is frass, the caterpillar's droppings, and finding it packed into the whorl is the identifying sign.

Confirm it before treating:

- Open the whorl on several plants across the field, early morning or late evening when the larvae are active.
- The larva has a pale upside-down Y marking on the head capsule.
- There are four dark spots arranged in a square near the tail end.

Count affected plants out of twenty. That proportion, not the presence of one caterpillar, is what decides whether treatment is worth the cost.
How do I tell groundnut rosette apart from other problems on groundnut?

Groundnut rosette on groundnut can be identified in the field before you treat.

What to look for:
- Stunted bushy plants with small distorted yellowed leaves, often in patches within the field.

Carried by aphids, worst in late planted and sparse stands. Plant early and at a dense even spacing so the canopy closes quickly, and use resistant varieties where available. Check this against what your neighbours are seeing before you act on a whole field.
What is the right way to use mulch on my plots?

Mulch keeps soil moist between rains, holds soil temperature down and suppresses weeds, which on a vegetable plot can be worth more than an extra watering. It also protects the surface from the impact of heavy rain, which is what starts erosion. Crop residues, cut grass and leaves all work; the point is covering the ground. If what you see in the field does not match this, take a sample to an extension officer rather than guessing.
My poultry is showing damage and I suspect coccidiosis. How do I be sure?

Coccidiosis on poultry can be identified in the field before you treat.

What to look for:
- Blood in droppings, huddling, ruffled feathers, poor growth.

Wet caked litter is the driver. Fixing litter and ventilation prevents recurrence better than repeated medication. Ask the older farmers in your area what has worked there, since local experience beats a general rule.
